doc.title: Herbie Hancock interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 18, 1995

title: Playing inside the piano on tour with Corea
summary: Stunts like banging the piano harp, the Hamburg photo, the Montreux encore without pianos, and the 1976, 1978 and Brazil tours.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah. Exactly. So we started getting into playing inside the piano you know, and doing things like that, a combination of the two, and different effects, and then hitting, then we started hitting the sounding board and hitting the metal part, the harp of the piano, using that for rhythm. And I remember one concert, I think it was in Hamburg. We played the concert and the next morning the newspaper comes out and there’s a picture of Chick and I. Chick was in the piano, knees and everything. I mean he had crawled into the piano, I was under the piano on my back, banging on the sounding board, and we were actually, things had just gone that far. We were making music with rhythm using other parts of the piano. I mean it was amazing. We would use physical gestures sometimes. We’d get into where we were playing things and I’d do this, and then he would do this, or then he would do this. And then there were eye movements, you know. Up and down and you know, and that became part of it, and different things. And then you know he would do, but we would make it as though it were music. We’d make some kind of pattern, organized patterns out of it. And integrate that, those kind of body movements, with the notes that we were playing. And it made some sense. Once we played at the Montreaux Jazz Festival and this was incredible. We got so many standing ovations it was amazing. It got to the point where by the third or fourth or fifth standing ovation, we decided not to even go to the pianos. So I took a chair, set it down in the middle of the stage, Chick sat in the chair and I sat next to him, and we, for the last final encore, we never even touched the pianos. We were making sounds with our mouth, and doing things with gestures, and all kinds of things. And the people went crazy. They loved it. And because we had kind of gotten them to that. They were along for the trip. And it really worked. It was a great,

great thing to experience for me. And we wound up actually doing two tours. One was in ‘76 and I think the other one was in 1978. So we had a great time together. And then we did a, we actually did a short tour in Brazil, and I’ve forgotten what year that was, Brazil and some other parts of South America, in the ‘80s.
